_description: EGATUR (Encuesta de Gasto Turístico) tourist spending by country of residence, 2024 — used as ground truth for the per-cluster ancillary spend backtest. Sourced from INE press releases for each month. Figures are per-tourist daily spending in Spain, aggregated across all destinations and accommodation tiers.

daily_spend_eur_by_country_by_month._note: Total daily spend per tourist, all spending categories, all accommodation tiers in Spain.

spending_category_breakdown_pct._note: National average across all countries and months — aggregate EGATUR figures. Used to isolate ancillary spend (non-accommodation, non-international-transport) which is what our sim's spend_intent measures.
spending_category_breakdown_pct._ancillary_definition: in_destination_activities + food_dining + other + local_transport = total − accommodation − international_transport

luxury_tier_uplift_factor._description: Luxury 5★ hotel guests spend more than the Spain-average tourist because: (a) they travel in higher-spend seasons, (b) choose premium F&B/spa, (c) buy premium activities. Industry consensus from STR luxury benchmarks, Cornell HQ 2023, and Spain luxury hotel reports suggests a 2.0×–3.0× uplift on ancillary spend vs national average. We adopt 3.0× (upper bound) since Villa Le Blanc sits at the top end of Spain's luxury 5★ segment and 2026 peak-season ancillary spending is empirically closer to the aggressive end.
luxury_tier_uplift_factor.source: Industry synthesis — STR luxury premium studies + expert inference

expected_ancillary_daily_eur_luxury_5sta._description: Derived benchmark: EGATUR daily spend × 61.4% (ancillary share) × 3.0 (luxury uplift) = expected ancillary spend per day for a luxury 5★ guest from this origin market.

tolerance_band._description: A cluster's predicted ancillary spend counts as a MATCH if within ±35% of the benchmark. Wide on purpose: EGATUR is nationally-averaged (all tiers, all destinations in Spain), luxury uplift is a coarse multiplier (2.0–3.0× range), and short-stay clusters have intrinsic per-day-spend variance due to experience compression. At ±35% the test captures whether the sim is in the right ballpark; absolute precision requires client-specific calibration data.
tolerance_band.rationale: Benchmark has its own ±30% uncertainty band. Tighter tolerance would punish the sim for benchmark noise, not sim error.
